---
name: pr-re-review
description: "Manually re-review a GitHub pull request after new commits or review-thread replies. Reassess earlier human and bot feedback, reply with verified status and diff context, and add new inline review findings without duplicating earlier rounds."
---

# PR re-review

Use this skill when asked to re-review, follow up on review comments, or check a PR again after a push or review-thread discussion. This is an **independent review**, not a request to GitHub's built-in Copilot reviewer. Accept a PR URL or `owner/repo#number`; if already in a PR session, use its PR. Do not run automatically or post to a PR the user did not identify. Never modify the PR's code or resolve/unresolve its threads as part of this skill.

## Read a complete snapshot

1. Resolve repository, PR number, base and current head SHA, author, changed-file list and full current base-to-head diff. Fetch all pages of commits (and compare commits since the last completed round), reviews, inline review comments **including replies**, and conversation comments; inspect current thread resolution/outdated status when the API supplies it. Use available GitHub tools first. If they cannot read all pages or required fields, use authenticated `gh api --paginate` / `gh pr diff` or an equivalent authenticated GitHub API; do not mistake issue comments for inline review comments. The relevant REST routes are `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}`, `/pulls/{number}/files`, `/pulls/{number}/commits`, `/pulls/{number}/reviews`, `/pulls/{number}/comments`, and `/issues/{number}/comments`. A file `patch` may be absent/truncated: obtain the full PR diff or stop short of commenting on that location. Do not silently review a partial diff.
2. Group inline comments into threads by following each reply's `in_reply_to_id` to its **top-level review comment ID**. Read the root, every reply, author, timestamps, original hunk/position, and latest code, including outdated or resolved threads. Fetch code beyond the diff when needed to understand behavior. Treat thread claims as evidence to verify, not proof. Ignore purely social or non-actionable discussion for status posting, but retain its context.
3. Read all earlier `pr-re-review` markers and comments on this PR, including pending reviews. Use a completed marker to locate the last reviewed head and discussion snapshot. The first run has no prior marker and reviews the entire PR. A round is needed if the head changed or the external review-discussion fingerprint changed. Compute that fingerprint from the sorted `(comment ID, updated_at, body)` of **non-skill** inline roots/replies, substantive review bodies, and substantive PR conversation comments (exclude this skill's own tagged review bodies, comments, and replies); use a digest or a stable canonical representation. Edits to existing replies and conversation comments must count. Do not use timestamps alone, local state, or just the latest commit. If neither head nor external discussion changed, report "no new activity" without posting.
4. Freeze `head`, discussion fingerprint, and previous completed marker as the round input. Generate a stable round ID from PR identity and those values. Before writing, re-fetch the head and external discussion fingerprint; if either changed, refresh the snapshot and re-review rather than publishing stale findings. The skill's own posts must not self-trigger another round.

## Review and reconcile

- On every new head, examine the changes since the previous completed round **and** the full current PR diff with the relevant surrounding code and tests. Look for regressions, missed actionable issues and fixes to old findings. A reply-only round still reassesses every substantive thread against the current code; additionally address the new reply. Avoid repeating unrelated findings from previous rounds.
- For each substantive thread, classify the underlying finding as **fixed**, **still open**, or **cannot verify**. A moved or deleted line is not automatically a fix; trace the behavior to its current location. Quote concrete evidence: current path/line and head SHA, and the correct current diff hunk if available. Say why a proposed fix does or does not address the behavior. Post one concise status reply per thread per round, even if the thread was previously resolved; never change its resolution state.
- Deduplicate new findings against all existing roots, replies and proposed posts by underlying cause, not simply line number. If an issue belongs to an existing thread, add it as a reply there rather than starting another thread. For a genuinely distinct issue, write a concise actionable finding with an accurate, short `diff` fenced excerpt copied from the **current** patch; identify the failure path and suggested correction. Only create a new inline comment when the anchor exists in the current PR diff (correct file path, blob line, `RIGHT` for additions/context or `LEFT` for deletions, and correct multiline start/end when used). Review comment APIs create the diff anchor; including a `diff` excerpt in the body supplies human-readable context but is not a substitute for an anchor. For a finding with no valid inline anchor, disclose it in the review summary instead of inventing a line or posting a misleading file comment.
- A reply attaches to the original top-level review comment, even when that comment is outdated; a reply **does not** move the anchor. Add a verified current diff excerpt to a still-open reply when it helps locate the surviving problem. For a fixed finding with no current hunk, cite current code instead of quoting an old hunk as current. Label uncertainty honestly.

## Publish exactly one round

Use an unobtrusive marker in each post, for example `<!-- pr-re-review:v1 round=<stable-id> kind=<status|finding|review|complete> -->`. The final completion marker is a PR conversation comment containing the round ID, reviewed head SHA, external discussion fingerprint, previous completed round ID, and counts/links for statuses and new findings. Markers are not a reason to skip reading the real discussion.

1. Prepare all candidate posts first. Recheck frozen head and external fingerprint immediately before the first write, and list posts/reviews for the round ID before every publication phase. Reuse already-posted items after a retry; do not double-post. If another actor advanced the head, stop publication, report any partial posts, and redo the review at the new head. If external replies or substantive conversation comments arrive **after writing began**, finish the frozen round only if the head is unchanged; record the **frozen** fingerprint so the next invocation processes that later discussion. Do not silently incorporate late discussion into a round already being published.
2. For new distinct inline findings, create **one pending review**, add precisely anchored comments with the verified current diff excerpt, then submit it once as `COMMENT` with a concise round summary. Use `pull_request_review_write` (`create`, then `submit_pending`) and `add_comment_to_pending_review` if available; otherwise use the corresponding REST review endpoints. Recover an existing pending review for this round instead of opening another. Do not approve or request changes by default. If there are no new inline findings, omit the pending review.
3. Reply to each substantive thread's **root numeric review-comment ID** with the classification, evidence, and round marker; `add_reply_to_pull_request_comment` or `POST /pulls/{number}/comments/{root_id}/replies` is appropriate. Do not reply to a reply ID. Post one completion summary/marker to the PR conversation **last**, after verifying the head is still the reviewed SHA and every intended comment exists. Summarize fixed/still-open/unverifiable/new findings and any findings lacking inline anchors.
4. If any API call, permission check, pagination, or validation fails, stop and report the exact unposted items. Do not write a completion marker. On retry, inspect this round's marker-tagged comments and pending/submitted reviews, reconcile actual GitHub state, and publish only missing items. Never claim a complete review on partial data or assume a timed-out write failed before checking whether its marker appeared.

## Checks before finishing

Verify the review is attached to the intended PR/head; every reply belongs to its original root; each new inline comment's path/line/side is present in the current diff and its quoted hunk matches; there is at most one status reply per thread and one new comment per finding per round; the completion marker is present only for a fully published round. Report the reviewed SHA, round status and links. Do not run live posting as a validation exercise: validate formatting and workflow with mock fixtures or a specifically authorized test PR.

## Example round sequence

- First invocation on `owner/repo#42` at head `H1`, with substantive roots `101` and `102`: inspect both full threads and the entire diff, post one justified status reply per root, add any distinct anchored findings, then record completed round `R1` for `H1` and the frozen external discussion fingerprint.
- A push to `H2` and a human reply under `101`: compare new commits, inspect the whole current diff and both threads, reply to roots `101` and `102` with their current status, and record `R2` after publication. A new defect that elaborates root `101` goes in that thread; a different defect on a changed line gets a new inline review comment quoting the actual `H2` hunk.
- Another human reply under `102` without a push: re-evaluate both substantive threads against `H2`, publish only that round's responses, and record `R3`. Immediately invoking the skill again with the same head and external fingerprint posts nothing.
- If posting `R3` stops after one reply, the retry finds its round tag, posts only missing items and then marks completion. If `H3` arrives during review, start a fresh snapshot before posting; if it arrives during publication, report partial `H2` output and review `H3` on the next attempt. A line that moved or vanished must be traced in current code, not assumed fixed or anchored to a nonexistent hunk.
